case: Domain-over-enum NULLIF refusal and qualified base-enum control under shadowed search_path
contract: The raw NULLIF(domain_column, $1) form is refused by PostgreSQL with SQLSTATE 42883, consistent with the domain-to-unknown operator boundary.
Casting the domain column to its qualified base enum permits NULLIF to infer text and SQL NULL parameters as the target enum even when search_path selects a same-named shadow enum.
Matching, non-matching, literal NULL-label and SQL NULL behavior are asserted with pg_typeof checks for the parameter, expression result and original domain column.
An invalid enum label through the qualified base-enum control returns native SQLSTATE 22P02, and all source values/types remain unchanged.

native_contract.command: rtk proxy cargo test --manifest-path linux/Cargo.toml -p tablepro-driver-postgres --test integration domain_contract::value_contract_domain_over_enum_nullif_infers_parameter_type -- --include-ignored --exact --nocapture --test-threads=1

native_domain_contract_group.command: rtk proxy cargo test --manifest-path linux/Cargo.toml -p tablepro-driver-postgres --test integration domain_contract:: -- --include-ignored --test-threads=1

clippy.command: rtk proxy cargo clippy --manifest-path linux/Cargo.toml -p tablepro-driver-postgres --all-targets -- -D warnings

remaining: Other domain depths and session/search_path configurations remain untested; raw domain-to-unknown NULLIF remains an explicit refusal and requires a qualified base-enum cast in the tested contract.
